children: New Delhi, Nov. 10 -- November also marks the beginning of winter and in northern India, the drop in temperature can make early mornings and late evenings quite chilly and uncomfortable as well. If you are planning to buy a room heater, it is worth comparing options before the colder weeks arrive. At a budget of under Rs.3,000, you will mostly find compact heaters designed for smaller rooms or personal heating, rather than appliances meant to warm large spaces. We have picked five room heaters listed on Amazon from Havells, Crompton, Orient Electric and Amazon Basics. Here is what their features, limitations and customer feedback tell you.

If you need warmth around your desk or bedside, a quartz heater offers a fairly simple approach: it directs radiant heat towards the area in front of it. The Havells Bero uses two quartz heating tubes and offers two power settings. Its compact format and carry handle also make it easier to move between rooms when needed.

Customers appreciate the heater's design and overall build quality. However, feedback on heating performance is divided, with some finding the heat output weak. Reliability, durability and value for money also receive mixed responses, including reports of the heater stopping after a short period.

The Bero is a pretty decent option for someone who wants targeted warmth without a bulky appliance. Its two quartz tubes and 400W/800W settings make it worth considering for a desk, bedside or small seating area.

The Crompton Comfy Plus is another quartz heater, but it adds a few practical touches for everyday use. Its 800W heating element has two heat settings, while the rust-resistant reflector is designed to maintain heat reflection. A tip-over switch cuts power if the heater falls, and the carry handle makes repositioning easier.

Customers find the heater comfortable to use in smaller rooms, including bedrooms. However, opinions on heating performance and value are mixed. Reliability and durability are concerns in some feedback, with buyers reporting units failing after limited use.

The Comfy Plus keeps things uncomplicated with two quartz heating levels, a portable design and tip-over protection. It is worth comparing if you want a simple heater for a smaller space rather than whole-room temperature control.

Unlike the quartz models above, the Orient Electric Areva uses a blower to distribute warm air. The current official Areva model offers two heating modes, 1000W and 2000W, and can be positioned horizontally or vertically. Its compact body, built-in handle and five-level protection are useful additions for moving and operating it around the house.

Customers praise the heater's heating performance, with some saying the temperature rises within three to five minutes. However, functionality and value receive mixed feedback. Noise is a recurring concern, while some buyers report durability problems and say the heater stopped working within a month.

The Areva's 1000W and 2000W modes give it more flexibility than the lower-powered quartz options. It is worth considering if you prefer fan-assisted heating and want an appliance that can be positioned in two orientations.

The Amazon Basics convection heater takes a different route from the quartz models in this list. It uses a 2000W heating system and offers two heat settings, making it a higher-powered option for indoor use. Its compact form is useful if you have limited floor space, although the actual heating experience will depend on the room's size and insulation.

Customers appreciate the heater's compact size and say it provides adequate warmth, including in chilly workspaces. Value for money also receives positive feedback. However, opinions on performance are mixed, with some buyers finding it effective and others saying it does not heat sufficiently.

The 2000W convection setup makes this a different proposition from the lower-powered quartz heaters. It is worth considering if you want a compact appliance that circulates warm air rather than providing only direct radiant heat.

The Havells HeatKing is a convector room heater designed for users who want adjustable heating rather than direct radiant warmth. It offers two power settings of 900W and 1800W, allowing you to choose the heating level according to the room and weather conditions. The compact design, weighing approximately 1.532kg, also makes it easier to move around the house. Its ISI certification is another important consideration for home use.
Amazon's customer summary reflects neutral feedback across product quality, heating performance, value for money, reliability and effectiveness.

The HeatKing stands out with its convector heating system and adjustable 900W and 1800W settings. It is worth considering if you want to switch between lower and higher heating levels while keeping the appliance compact.
